_note: The Foundation home base as DATA — GDD §13, cut to the compact five-room slice of §26.2: operations room, armory/logistics counter, archive terminal, small research station, containment observation corridor. §13.1 asks that preparing for a mission take minutes and not a commute, so this is a screen with tabs rather than a walkable building, and every room is one page. The eight core areas of §13.2 are folded into five: the research station carries the isolation bench that a full site would give the Medical Wing, and the logistics counter carries the Engineering Bay's repair queue. That is not a shortcut, it is the fiction — an underfunded regional facility has one room doing three jobs, and §13.3 says the site begins underfunded.
_effectsNote: Every `effect` key is validated against DEFAULT_EFFECTS in src/sim/progression.js and the file REFUSES to load if it names one no system reads. An upgrade that quietly did nothing would fail §13.3's 'upgrades visibly add capability' without ever failing a test.
standing: Regional Site 19 runs on a regional grant, one vehicle, and whatever the last operation brought back. Nothing here is new and two of the rooms were something else first.

regionalStatus.weather: Overcast, 4C, wind from the north-east. No change expected before the window closes.
regionalStatus.region: Three counties, one duty squad, and a coroner who has stopped asking questions.
regionalStatus.readiness: One vehicle. One command point. Everything you take is everything you have.

rooms.name: Operations room
rooms.purpose: Where an incident becomes an operation. The board, the map table, the regional picture, and the readiness check that says whether the squad can actually go.
rooms.furniture: A map table with a cracked overlay, a wall board, and a radio set that predates the site.
allows: Read the mission board and take the authorised operation
Read the regional and weather picture before committing
Check squad readiness, including who is carrying an injury

upgrades.name: Backup power
upgrades.blurb: A generator and a proper charging bench. Cells go out full instead of go out.
upgrades.visible: The corridor lights stop dropping when the compressor cycles, and every issued item leaves with an extra minute on it.

upgrades.name: Additional vehicle bay
upgrades.blurb: A second vehicle means the manifest stops being a single wager.
upgrades.visible: Two more volume on every cargo manifest, for good.

rooms.name: Armory and logistics counter
rooms.purpose: Loadouts, maintenance, the cargo manifest, and equipment recovery. The counter is also the repair queue, because there is no engineering bay and the same person does both.
rooms.furniture: A roller shutter, a parts bin, and a whiteboard listing what did not come back.
allows: Fit an equipment sidegrade, or refit the standard tool
Requisition new variants against department standing
Read what the last operation failed to recover

upgrades.name: Specialised storage
upgrades.blurb: Climate-controlled racking with sensor ports, and a bonded cage for recovered gear.
upgrades.visible: Two more holding positions in the corridor, and written-off equipment costs a quarter less to reorder.

rooms.name: Archive terminal
rooms.purpose: Case files, mission history, the anomaly codex, and the attribution record. One terminal, one chair, and everything the site has ever filed.
rooms.furniture: A terminal on a desk that was a canteen table.
allows: Read the debrief history, dimension by dimension
Read the case file on anything the site has encountered
Read the attribution and licensing record

upgrades.name: Expanded archives
upgrades.blurb: Proper indexing and a second terminal, so a case file can be cross-read against the last twenty operations.
upgrades.visible: Twenty operations on file instead of twelve, and a tenth more analytical yield from everything you bring back.

upgrades.name: Training and simulation space
upgrades.blurb: A room with a floor plan taped out on it and a procedure rehearsal each week. Departments notice a squad that practises.
upgrades.visible: Every standing gain is worth about a sixth more.

rooms.name: Research station
rooms.purpose: Sample analysis, research projects, and the isolation bench the site uses to treat exposure because there is no medical wing.
rooms.furniture: A fume hood, a sample fridge, and one isolation bed behind a curtain.
allows: Spend research data on prototypes and analytical unlocks
Read what the site knows about an anomaly, and what it would take to know more
Treat an injured operative, or decide not to and field them anyway

upgrades.name: Better medical isolation
upgrades.blurb: A second bed, a real airlock, and a supply cupboard that is not shared with the sample fridge.
upgrades.visible: Two operatives can be treated in the same rotation, and a course costs less than half again.

rooms.name: Containment observation corridor
rooms.purpose: A short run of cells and monitor feeds. Whatever the site is holding is held here, and the corridor's job is to record what holding it costs.
rooms.furniture: Three cells, a monitor bank with one dead channel, and a clipboard nobody has replaced with a tablet.
allows: Read the operational history of everything in custody
Read the maintenance record and what the next check is due
See which holding positions are free before committing to an operation

upgrades.name: Stronger perimeter monitoring
upgrades.blurb: Sensors on the corridor and the fence line, reporting continuously instead of when somebody walks past.
upgrades.visible: Checks fall due two operations further apart, and the regional grant goes up because the auditors can see the logs.

operations.name: Cold storage, level 2
operations.distance: Forty minutes out. Sub-level, no surface exposure.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of the anomaly on level 2 and transfer it to the stair head.
conditions: Mains down six days. Two circuits, both dead.
One surviving crew member waiting at the stair head.
Plant log reports the chiller ran eleven days against a four-hour duty cycle.

operations.name: Cold storage, aisle B
operations.distance: The same floor as the last one. You already know the way.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of the figure reported in aisle B and transfer it to the stair head.
optional: Preserve a dust sample from the ring
conditions: Repeat sighting, four calls in one shift, nothing found on four walks.
The supervisor watched it on camera instead and it stayed put for six hours.
Fourteen unexplained brownouts on the storage circuit, none over nine seconds.
operations._note: The SAME MAP as op-cold-storage-2 and a completely different operation — GDD 15.2's epistemic and operational variation. The board is the one place a player sees that the building is a constant and the incident is the variable.

operations.name: Ashlar House, ninth floor
operations.distance: Two hours out, then nine floors on foot. The lift is out and the stair is the only way anything leaves.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of the anomaly on the ninth floor and transfer it to the east landing.
optional: Recover the contractor day book intact
conditions: Condemned crosswall block, decanted eleven months, stripped back to the frame.
Both circuits are on the contractor temporaries. Nothing is locked; everything is stuck open.
The drained district-heating gallery runs the full width of the floor behind the store rooms.
operations._note: THE SAME ANOMALY as op-cold-storage-2, on different geometry — the mirror of what the aisle B operation does. GDD 15.2 varies the incident against a constant building; this varies the building against a constant incident, and a squad that arrives with the cold store playbook has brought the right tools in the wrong quantity to the wrong end of a very long walk.

operations.name: Cold storage, the stocktake
operations.distance: The same forty minutes, the same stair, the third time.
operations.mandate: Recover the discrepancy in full, verify the count against the stocktake, and transfer it to the stair head.
optional: Log nothing into the case that does not belong there
Read the second clerk's sheet before committing to a count
conditions: Two independent stocktakes returned the same wrong number.
Nothing on this floor has been reported as moving, and nobody has been hurt.
The clerk who ran the second count is at the stair head and has her sheet.
operations._note: THE THIRD FAMILY (GDD 26.2: distributed-object recovery and verification) and the third operation on this one floor. Nothing hunts you here, there is no fence, and the failure state is arithmetic. A squad that has done the other two walks in knowing where the breakers are and which aisle is long, and none of that is the answer — familiarity is the trap.

_boardNote: Three operations, and every one of them is playable to custody — the board does not pad itself with contracts that do not exist. §18.1 does not allow the UI to lie about what is available, so a greyed-out fourth entry would be a promise this build cannot keep. Two of the three share a floor and two of the three share an anomaly, which is the whole of §15.2 in three rows: the building is a variable and the incident is a variable, and they vary independently.

containmentWing.framing: Entries record where it came from, what holding it costs, and what it has done since. They do not rank captures, do not count them as a score, and do not describe anything held here as a prize. An object in a cell is an ongoing operational commitment, not a result.
maintenanceNotes: Scheduled check. Cell log reviewed against the sensor bus; no discrepancy recorded.
Interior temperature drifted 0.4C over the interval. Within tolerance, logged, watched.
Monitor channel two reported a two-second dropout. Cause not established. Cell inspected and re-sealed.
Consumable draw above forecast for the interval. Requisition notified.

cells.label: Cell 1
cells.holding: Insulated, heated, sensor ports on the corridor bus. The only position rated for a thermal negative.

cells.label: Cell 2
cells.holding: General holding. Sealed door, one camera, no environmental control.

cells.label: Cell 3
cells.holding: Locker-scale. Objects and samples, not organisms. The extract fan has been on the list since March.

dossiers._designationNote: A provisional internal designation, not an SCP number. GDD §25.3 holds that a final designation is assigned only after the licensing record exists, and content/anomalies/graybox-draught.json carries `licensingRecordId: null`. Nothing in this build should print a number it has not earned the right to print.
dossiers.classFraming: A thermal negative that moves toward heat and cannot cross a sustained gradient above 40C. Not hostile in any sense the site can evidence; it is cold, and people are warm.
dossiers.holding: escort at 39C in a heated transit case, corridor cleared, two operatives
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs a heated cell on continuous draw and a fortnightly gradient check. It has never tested the seal. It has never had to.

insights.text: Thermal is the only reliable observation channel. It records faithfully in that band and not at all in the visible one, so a camera that sees nothing is not evidence of absence.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: The gradient figure is 40C, sustained and continuous. A contour with a gap in it is not a fence, and the aisles on level 2 are 4.2m across.
insights.grants: The figure appears on the briefing instead of being inferred in the field.

insights.text: It goes to the warmest thing it can reach. A transit case held one degree under the threshold out-competes an operative; a tripod set down too near the case takes the case over the threshold and the lure stops working.
insights.grants: The archive files this as a procedure note rather than a hard-won field lesson.

_insightNote: Insights grant CONTEXT ONLY — a line the briefing did not previously carry. None of them changes a number the anomaly obeys, because GDD §12.1 says progression must not turn horror into immunity. A squad that has read all three still has to build the fence.
